cf.title: walreceiver: stale hot_standby_feedback xmin on primary when wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 (PG16 and later)

input.subject: walreceiver: stale hot_standby_feedback xmin on primary when wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 (PG16 and later)

verdict_reasoning: The bug is reproduced and the goal is not in dispute. The open point is which interval-0 behaviour back branches should get: replication-ondisk-1 shows that the patched build invalidates logical slots on a standby that work today, and standards-compat-2 shows the choice of "feedback off" over the 15 behaviour is not argued. maintenance-fit-2 adds that slotsync still accepts interval 0. The list should agree on the semantics before code review.

brief.title: Walreceiver: release primary xmin when wal_receiver_status_interval is 0
brief.problem: With hot_standby_feedback = on and wal_receiver_status_interval = 0, Postgres 16 and later send one feedback message with a valid xmin at connect or reload, then nothing more. The primary keeps that xmin until the next reconnect, and VACUUM on the primary cannot remove dead rows. Postgres 14 and 15 are not affected.
brief.proposed_design: The walreceiver computes an xmin only when hot_standby_feedback is on and wal_receiver_status_interval > 0, so with interval 0 it sends InvalidTransactionId and the primary releases the xmin. This makes interval 0 mean "no hot standby feedback", which matches the existing early return and wakeup logic. A new TAP test in src/test/recovery checks the slot xmin and is meant for back-patching to 16.
user_visible_surface: Changed behaviour: hot_standby_feedback = on with wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 now sends no xmin, so the primary holds no xmin or catalog_xmin for the standby.
author_claims: The bug affects 16, 17, 18, 19 and master, and the same code change applies to all of them.
The fix keeps the documented meaning that 0 disables status updates.
The new TAP test fails without the fix and passes with it, without timing races.
Postgres 14 and 15 keep advancing the xmin with interval 0, because their once-per-interval check is always true.
brief.thread_state: Joao Rito reviewed v2 on master, confirmed the bug and the fix, and asked which interval-0 behaviour is intended, since 15 kept sending feedback and the patch sends none. He also reported that logical slots on a standby get invalidated with the fix, and asked for doc changes and possibly a warning or a slotsync check.
unclear: The proposal does not say why "feedback off" was chosen over restoring the Postgres 15 behaviour of sending feedback on every call.
The patch does not change config.sgml to say that interval 0 disables hot standby feedback.
The proposal does not address logical slots on the standby, and synced slots, that lose catalog_xmin protection with interval 0.
The proposal does not say whether a release note or a warning is planned for users who run with interval 0 in a minor release.
The stale xmin left when the walreceiver connects before Hot Standby is active is deferred to a separate thread.

prior_attempts.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
prior_attempts.quote: I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.
prior_attempts.reason: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P8 changed how invalidated physical slots are accepted. This patch changes what hot standby feedback sends with interval 0, but it also changes shipped slot behaviour in back branches.

objections.title: Back-patch makes a minor release invalidate logical slots on standbys
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 16 to 19 runs hot_standby_feedback = on and wal_receiver_status_interval = 0, with a logical slot or synced failover slot on the standby. After a minor update the primary drops catalog_xmin and catalog VACUUM removes rows. The standby logs "invalidating obsolete replication slot", decoding fails, and the subscriber must be rebuilt.
objections.argument: Message #4, case 5, shows this invalidation with the patch and not without it. Today the stale catalog_xmin protects the slot, even if only as a side effect of the bug. The patch is marked Backpatch-through: 16, but it adds no release note, no warning, and no slotsync.c check that rejects interval 0. A committer would likely be wary of a minor release that breaks replication setups which work today, as the recorded concern in [P8] about changing long-released slot behaviour shows.
objections.author_must_show: How will users with standby logical or synced slots and interval 0 be protected or warned before a minor update invalidates those slots?

precedents.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.

critic.reasoning: Message #4, case 5, shows the invalidation on the patched build only, and the patch is marked Backpatch-through: 16 with no release note or warning. [P8] is weak support, because that entry was returned after its author stopped replying.

objections.title: Interval 0 gets a third meaning, silently overriding hot_standby_feedback
objections.failure_scenario: A user upgrading from 15 keeps hot_standby_feedback = on and wal_receiver_status_interval = 0, which sent feedback on every call there. On 16+ with the patch, the standby sends no xmin and logs nothing. The user finds out from query cancellations on the standby or from slotsync running without catalog_xmin protection.
objections.argument: Message #1 shows that 14 and 15 sent feedback on every call with interval 0, so the patch fixes a third behaviour across branches. The proposal does not say why "feedback off" was preferred over restoring the 15 behaviour, which message #4 asked about. The hot_standby_feedback entry in config.sgml says only that feedback is not sent more often than once per interval, and the patch leaves the docs unchanged. Slotsync still accepts this combination without a check or a warning.
objections.author_must_show: Why should interval 0 disable feedback that the user turned on explicitly, instead of restoring the 15 behaviour, and where is the user told this happens?

critic.reasoning: The existing docs say interval 0 disables status updates, which supports the author's choice. But message #4 asked why the 15 behaviour was not restored and the thread has no answer, and the patch does not change config.sgml.

objections.title: Rule that interval 0 disables feedback is not enforced in one place
objections.failure_scenario: Slot synchronization checks only hot_standby_feedback, so a standby with interval 0 passes the check while the primary gets no catalog_xmin for synced slots. A later patch that reads hot_standby_feedback alone repeats the bug, and no test fails until a user loses slot protection.
objections.argument: The bug came from two copies of the "feedback enabled" test that disagreed. The patch adds a third copy in walreceiver.c and leaves slotsync.c and config.sgml unaware of the new rule (message #4, comments 2 to 4). Nothing fails loudly when the next caller checks only hot_standby_feedback. A single helper used by walreceiver and slotsync, plus a doc sentence, would close this gap.
objections.author_must_show: Will the patch define one "hot standby feedback is enabled" test that walreceiver and slotsync both use, and state the rule in config.sgml?

critic.reasoning: The helper in walreceiver.c is a code structure point, which message #4 calls a matter of taste. The slotsync check is a design gap: with the patch it accepts interval 0 while the primary gets no catalog_xmin for synced slots.

refuted.title: Back-patched change to interval 0 can invalidate standby logical slots
refuted.failure_scenario: A site on 17 runs hot_standby_feedback = on with wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 and has a logical slot or synced slot on the standby. After a minor update, the primary drops catalog_xmin and VACUUM removes catalog rows. The standby slot is invalidated, and decoding fails with "can no longer access replication slot".
refuted.argument: Message #4, case 5, reproduces this invalidation with v2, while unpatched master kept the slot usable. In [P8], a committer warned against changing behaviour that has shipped for several releases, and this patch changes the meaning of interval 0 in 16 to 19 in a minor release. Message #4, comment 1, also notes that restoring the 15 behaviour was an option that does not drop protection. The thread has no reply on this point, and the commit message picks "feedback off" without a reason.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should back branches get "interval 0 disables feedback" rather than the 15 behaviour, and what protects existing standby logical slots after the minor update?

precedents.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same slot invalidation and names the missing release note, warning and slotsync check. The question about the 15 behaviour is covered by standards-compat-2.

refuted.title: Back-patched fix removes xmin protection that existing standbys rely on
refuted.failure_scenario: A site on 16 runs hot_standby_feedback = on with wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 and a logical slot on the standby. After a minor update, the primary drops the slot's catalog_xmin, VACUUM removes catalog rows, and the standby slot is invalidated with rows_removed. They find out when decoding fails with "can no longer access replication slot".
refuted.argument: Message #4, case 5, reproduces this on the patched build, and the same setup works today. The patch is marked Backpatch-through: 16, so the change reaches users in a minor release without their asking. Standby queries that the stale xmin protected may also start to be cancelled. The commit message does not mention this effect and does not propose a release note.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is it acceptable for a minor release to invalidate logical slots on standbys that work today, and what release note or warning tells those users first?

precedents.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. The scenario and the evidence from message #4, case 5, are the same.

refuted.title: Choice of "no feedback" over restoring the 15 behaviour is not argued
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who ran hot_standby_feedback = on with interval 0 on 15 upgrades to a patched 16 or later release. The primary now gets no xmin from the standby, and long standby queries are cancelled with recovery conflicts. The user finds out from cancelled reports, and config.sgml does not mention the cause.
refuted.argument: Message #1 states that on 14 and 15 interval 0 sent feedback on every call. It keeps that combination working there, and the patch defines a third behaviour. Message #4 asks whether restoring the 15 behaviour was considered, and the thread has no answer. The patch does not change config.sgml, which says feedback is sent at most once per interval, so a reader can take 0 to mean no limit.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is turning feedback off for interval 0 better for standby users than restoring the 15 behaviour, and where will config.sgml say so?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which makes the same point about the unanswered 15-behaviour question and the unchanged config.sgml.

refuted.title: Back-patching "interval 0 means feedback off" breaks standby logical slots
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on 17 runs a standby with hot_standby_feedback = on, wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 and a logical slot used for decoding. After a minor update, the primary drops the slot's catalog_xmin and VACUUM of catalogs invalidates the standby slot. The user finds out when decoding fails with "can no longer access replication slot".
refuted.argument: Message #4, case 5, reproduces this invalidation with the patch, while unpatched master keeps the slot usable. The patch picks one of two fixes, "feedback off" or the Postgres 15 behaviour of sending on every call, and the proposal does not say why. A minor release that turns a working setup into slot invalidation is a change the back branches must keep. The commit message does not mention this, and no release note or warning is planned.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is "feedback off" safer to back-patch than restoring the Postgres 15 behaviour, given that the patched setup invalidates logical slots on the standby?

precedents.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1 for the slot invalidation and of standards-compat-2 for the choice between the two fixes.

refuted.title: Interval 0 becomes a second off-switch for hot standby feedback
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who upgraded from 15 runs hot_standby_feedback = on with wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 and applies the minor release. The primary then gets no xmin or catalog_xmin, so standby queries are cancelled and logical slots on the standby are invalidated, as message #4 case 5 shows. The user finds out from cancellations or the error "can no longer access replication slot".
refuted.argument: Postgres already has a setting that turns feedback off: hot_standby_feedback = off. With the patch, interval 0 silently overrides an explicit hot_standby_feedback = on, and the docs do not say so. Message #4 asked why the 15 behaviour, which kept the two settings independent, was not restored, and the thread has no answer yet. The author's view that the early return already treats 0 as disabled describes the 16 code, not the documented meaning of hot_standby_feedback.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should interval 0 override hot_standby_feedback = on in back branches, when hot_standby_feedback = off already disables feedback and 15 kept sending it?

precedents.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The point that interval 0 overrides an explicit hot_standby_feedback = on without a doc change is the same.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the xmin that the walreceiver sends in hot standby feedback, which controls slot xmin and catalog_xmin on the primary.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: No new GUC, but wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 gains the meaning "hot_standby_feedback is off".

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The patches are marked Backpatch-through: 16 and change what interval 0 does in a minor release.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The "feedback enabled" test now exists in three places in walreceiver.c, and slotsync checks only hot_standby_feedback.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why should interval 0 turn hot standby feedback off in 16 to 19, instead of restoring the 15 behaviour of sending feedback on every call?
What protects or warns users whose standby logical slots or synced slots are invalidated after the minor update, as message #4 case 5 shows?
Will the patch change config.sgml to say that wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 disables hot standby feedback even when hot_standby_feedback is on?
Should slot synchronization reject or warn about wal_receiver_status_interval = 0, since the primary then gets no catalog_xmin for synced slots?
Is a release note planned for the back branches, and should master and the back branches get the same behaviour?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the walreceiver feedback code, replication slot xmin handling and slot synchronization would have to own it. The visible thread shows the author and one reviewer, and no committer has spoken.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in four back branches: any report of invalidated standby logical slots or cancelled standby queries after the minor update. The owner also signs for the interval-0 semantics in all later releases.
committability.author_follow_up: The author rebased within four days and said a separate thread will cover the related stale-xmin case. The visible thread has no reply yet to the review in message #4.

priority.reason: Only standbys with hot_standby_feedback = on and wal_receiver_status_interval = 0 are affected, and the patch is one condition in walreceiver.c plus a TAP test. The bug holds back VACUUM on the primary, so it deserves a fix once the interval-0 behaviour and the back-patch effects are agreed.

provisional_note: The code and the TAP test were not read, so the stability of the test and the exact effect on primary_has_standby_xmin could not be checked. Message #4 is known only through the brief and the objections.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

Diagnosys-by: Andrey Borodin <x4mmm@yandex-team.ru>
Diagnosys-by: Michael Paquier <michael@paquier.xyz>
Diagnosys-by: Andres Freund <andres@anarazel.de>

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix cancelled queries when hot_standby_feedback = on
precedents_retrieved.summary: With hot_standby_feedback = on, standby queries still get cancelled when vacuum truncates a heap on the primary, because the AccessExclusiveLock taken for truncation is replayed on the standby. The final patch adds a new lock level, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCAL, that vacuum uses for heap truncation and that is not WAL-logged, so standby queries must tolerate concurrent truncation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that letting scans run during truncation leaves a race: concurrent scans can load to-be-truncated pages back into shared buffers before ftruncate, and reading past EOF on a standby can extend the relation. Alexander Korotkov agreed the patch had to be revised and sketched a new truncation design, but Robert Haas called it fragile and doubted it prevents stale buffers from being taken as valid. No new version followed, the existing patch failed initdb, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we ever have valid-looking buffers in shared_buffers after the corresponding data has been truncated away on disk, we've got to make sure that nobody ever confuses one of them with an actually-valid buffer.

precedents_retrieved.title: Replica sends an incorrect epoch in its hot standby feedback to the Master
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a bug in Postgres 9.6, 10 and 11 where a replica's nextXid can move backward during WAL replay in RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds, so hot standby feedback carries a wrong epoch and the master ignores the replica's xmin. The one-line fix advances nextXid only when the new value is higher, as similar code elsewhere does.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The withdrawal was not a rejection of the fix. The author registered the patch in the commitfest more than once, and David Steele marked the duplicate entries 2462 and 2463 as withdrawn. The visible messages show no objection, and Thomas Munro agreed the nextXid assignment looked wrong.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have marked the duplicate entries 2462 and 2463 as withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sending WAL receiver feedback regularly even if the receiver is under heavy load
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_basebackup -X stream and pg_receivexlog send status feedback only when the incoming WAL stream pauses, so a continuous stream on a loaded receiver can make the walsender end the connection with a replication timeout. The patch checks the feedback interval inside the receive loop and sends feedback when it has elapsed. Later versions call gettimeofday() only at each WAL segment boundary, and separate patches covered walreceiver.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Fujii Masao's concern about frequent gettimeofday() calls led to v4 and v5, which he called reasonable. His last review asked whether feedback should also be sent in synchronous mode before the timeout, and the thread shows no reply from the author before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Even if the timeout has not elapsed yet, if synchronous mode is true, we should
send feedback here?

precedents_retrieved.title: Move walreceiver state assignment (to WALRCV_STREAMING) in WalReceiverMain()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the assignment of walrcv->walRcvState to WALRCV_STREAMING from the start of WalReceiverMain() to the point after walrcv_startstreaming() returns true. The author said the current placement causes no known issue but is less accurate, since connecting to the primary can still fail after it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Euler Taveira was concerned that keeping the state at WALRCV_STARTING longer could let WalRcvStreaming() hit the hardcoded WALRCV_STARTUP_TIMEOUT and stop a walreceiver that is slow to connect. Michael Paquier agreed and noted that v1 skipped the restart case. The author fixed the restart case in v2, but CFbot then reported test failures, and he withdrew the patch because the current code causes no issues.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Couldn't it give up before starting if you apply your patch? My main concern is
due to a slow system, the walrcv_connect() took to long in WalReceiverMain()
and the code above kills the walreceiver while in the process to start it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes StartReplication() reject a physical replication slot that has already been invalidated, for example by max_slot_wal_keep_size, as the logical walsender already does. Without it a walsender can stream from an invalidated slot, move its restart_lsn forward, and pg_replication_slots shows it as valid while it protects neither WAL nor rows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be
better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some
releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix possible segfault in walreceiver
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixed a segfault in WakeupRecovery() caused by commit ac22929a26, which reset XLogCtl->recoveryWakeupLatch to NULL while walreceiver could still signal it. The POC took a spinlock to fetch the latch pointer, but only when the pointer could be reset to NULL concurrently.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch because he reverted the commits it fixed, ac22929a26 and 113d3591b8, as they had other issues. With those commits gone, the fix had nothing left to fix. No one objected to the patch itself.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Previously I added this patch to next CommitFest. But I reverted the commit
ac22929a26 and 113d3591b8 because those changes have other issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronous replay mode for avoiding stale reads on hot standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a synchronous_replay mode in which a commit on the primary waits until all available hot standbys have replayed it, and the primary grants time-limited leases to standbys. A standby without a valid lease rejects synchronous_replay transactions with a new error 40P02, so reads on standbys never miss a commit that has already returned on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message, from February 2019, is a rebase by the author, and the entry was withdrawn in July 2019. Open items still visible at that point included missing TAP tests, an unexplained replication protocol corruption bug, and design questions from Masahiko Sawada about the GUCs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin"
Reverted commit(s): Test that vacuum removes tuples older than OldestXmin
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit
machines where fewer rows should be required.

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of
Postgres with TIDStore used for dead TID storage by vacuum, this is only
being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent proposes the same fix. P4 is about feedback under heavy load, P3 and P5 are about the feedback epoch, and P23 is an unstable vacuum test. None of their recorded reasons applies here.
The bug itself is not in dispute. Both objections concern the chosen semantics and how they reach back branches.
The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire message or ABI. Only the xmin value in an existing feedback message changes.

The change only affects which xmin the walreceiver sends when hot_standby_feedback is on and wal_receiver_status_interval is 0. Both settings are set by the standby administrator, so no new privilege, exposure or path for an unprivileged user exists, and the fix reduces the bloat risk on the primary.
There is no hot-path cost, no new dependency and no fit issue. This is a small bugfix in core code.
The bug fix itself is not covered by any existing feature or extension. Setting a positive interval avoids the bug but does not fix it.

This is a bug fix, so the demand test applies weakly: the author and the reviewer in message #4 both reproduced vacuum being held back on 16 and later. The cost falls only on standbys set to wal_receiver_status_interval = 0, and the choice between the two interval-0 behaviours belongs to the design angle.
